arguments.heading: What happened at the argument

The government relies on the same precedent but interprets it differently.
Justice Scalia noted the government ignored a relevant later case.
the sides that brought the case claim the new law attaches new consequences to old offenses.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a 2004 statute applies to crimes committed before its passage. the sides that brought the case argue the law lacks clear retroactive language. The government contends the ban applies to all prior convictions.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case want the Court to limit the travel ban to post-2004 crimes.
The government wants the Court to apply the ban to pre-2004 offenses.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case argue the statute does not expressly mandate retroactive application.
